sourceProjection.basis: The 2026 Architectural Review sheet was visually inspected: its left side contains three top-down orthographic floor plans, while sections and the site plan are not extracted directly.

The embedded ground-, first- and second-floor plan images were extracted at their native pixel dimensions without rescaling; the source PDF's inverted Decode display for the first-floor JPEG was reapplied losslessly.

review: Architectural Review publishes the three plans with credit to Arxiu ETSAB / Catedra Gaudi / ETSAB / UPC. The ground-floor caption explicitly says after Gaudi's interventions, and the sheet labels the first and second floors separately. The extracted source pages preserve all plan pixels but omit the publication page's overlaid numeric legend and unrelated sections; canonical place labels therefore retain the publication's exact printed identifiers 1 through 9, including two distinct occurrences of 9. These are treated as historical post-intervention architectural records, not a current visitor map. The earlier master-plan red overlay remains research evidence only because its legend does not separate retained construction from demolition sufficiently to reconstruct a complete phase. Native source/wall/detail contacts were reviewed after the shared source-only morphology fix. The main- and second-floor surfaces are exact locked white connected components from the source rasters; no ground-floor surface is asserted because its entry/lobby whites connect to the page exterior, and no terrace surface is asserted through the paving grid. On the main floor, 73 disconnected morphology remnants inside four locked paving, hatching and stair-detail regions are reclassified as flat detail using their exact source-component bounds. Five retained-wall probes lock the terrace perimeter, curved east wall, central enclosure and street facade.
limitations: 本模型仅重建来源明确绘出的底层、主层与二层；它们是高迪改造后的历史建筑平面，不是当前访客地图。
阁楼、龙脊屋顶、现行三层住宅、地下 Gaudi Cube 与 Gaudi Dome 均缺少可核验的完整正投影平面，因此不绘制、不绑定；官网列出的现行三层 12 个房间只保留为未定位语义清单。
主层与二层只填充来源实际闭合的室内连通面；底层入口/门厅与页外白底相连，主层后露台被铺地网格分割，均不封口补面。
铺地、楼梯踏步、家具及装饰线保持为平面细节；主层 73 个误入墙类的孤立细线交点已按来源连通分量精确降为细部，露台边墙、中央楼梯围护与街道立面仍由锁定采样保留。
母页嵌图变换支持三层采用近似相同出版比例，但裁切范围与轻微旋转不同；各层保持独立原点，不宣称测量级竖向配准。

scaleRelation.basis: The parent PDF embeds the ground, first and second plan rasters with transform-vector scales of 0.239954/0.239881, 0.239857/0.239529 and 0.239935/0.239670 PDF points per source pixel (horizontal/vertical). The maximum spread is about 0.15 percent. Repeated central stair and light-well geometry corroborates orientation, but different source crop extents and slight page rotations do not establish a common origin.
scaleRelation.registration: No cross-floor translation or survey-grade vertical registration is asserted.

research.finding: 2026 Architectural Review drawing sheet supplies native embedded ground-, first- and second-floor plans; plans are credited to Arxiu ETSAB / Catedra Gaudi / ETSAB / UPC.

Master-plan paper documents the building and reproduces black Emili Sala / red Antoni Gaudi intervention overlays, but the reviewed figure does not encode a separate demolition convention; it cannot define a complete post-intervention floor by colour union.
Ten-page Casa Batllo monograph excerpt contains photographs, text and a facade sketch but no complete indoor floor plan.

The broader Triangle Gaudi-building excerpt was downloaded and searched page by page. It includes Casa Batllo attic and roof photographs in its visual catalogue but no orthographic upper-floor, attic or roof plan.
UPC catalogue records Gaudi's signed 1904 basement, ground- and first-floor sheet at 1:100; the principal image is access-restricted by heritage policy.
UPC catalogue records the 1904 upper-floor, facade and section sheet; the principal image is access-restricted and was not used.

The Antonio Gaudi Foundation reproduces the 1904 permit drawings for a fifth floor and roof service rooms, but explicitly states that the attic configuration shown differs from what was built and notes other major unexecuted details. The permit roof/attic geometry is therefore unsuitable for the current visitor model.

The 2010 peer-reviewed accessibility paper (DOI 10.18848/1833-1874/CGP/v04i01/37839) is indexed as describing the then-visit and labels Image 10 as roof and attic visit routes. ResearchGate's author-copy endpoint was blocked, CGScholar article edition 2295 requires purchase and denied its download endpoint, and OpenAlex exposes no open-access copy. The indexed figure is a route diagram rather than a complete current architectural survey, so no geometry was extracted.
Current official experience page verifies visitor areas including the main floor, rear facade and courtyard, attic, rooftop and basement experience, but publishes no orthographic plans.
Current official ticket page verifies rooftop access, a temporary second-floor exhibition and an optional third-floor residence, but publishes no floor geometry.
Official memory booklet is photographic and provides no orthographic indoor plan.

The current official events page confirms the attic and Dragon Rooftop as a paired venue offer, but supplies photographs and capacity context rather than an orthographic floor plan or boundary drawing.

Casa Batllo's official attic events page identifies the attic as the former service, storage and laundry level, states that it is rented jointly with the roof and gives a 240 square metre event area. It provides photographs, a longitudinal section and a virtual-tour link, not a top-down boundary or room plan; the linked legacy virtual tour returned an access denial during review.

The official image exposed by the attic events page was fetched at its native 1200 by 675 pixels and visually inspected. Despite Planol in the filename, it is a longitudinal building section labelled TERRAT, GOLFES and PLANTA NOBLE / PATI MODERNISTA, not an orthographic floor plan. It supports vertical level semantics only and is not traced as a floor or stop face.

Casa Batllo's official 2026 Private Rooms site identifies twelve named rooms on the restored third floor and gives their individual areas. It publishes room photographs but no plan, adjacency, orientation or relative coordinates; the rooms therefore remain unlocated and are not added as places, spaces or stop bindings.

The official history page says the third floor began as rental apartments F and G in 1906, one residence expanded to three quarters of the floor in 1917, a two-year restoration began in 2023 and the floor opened to new uses in 2026. This establishes changing scope and date but gives no reconstructable plan.

The image referenced near the official third-floor material was downloaded and visually inspected at native size. It is a four-photograph room collage, not the plan implied by its page CSS class, and supplies no floor geometry.

Laia Pouget Mas's 2024 UPC architecture thesis La coberta com a paisatge was downloaded in full and pages 76-77 were visually inspected. It documents a rectangular roof divided centrally by interior-courtyard skylights, a front water-tank room and four chimney groups, and includes a longitudinal section and current roof photograph, but no attic or roof orthographic plan. These statements are retained as semantics only and do not support a floor boundary or stop face.

The 2024 English preview of Casa Batllo, Light & Colour was reviewed. It contains attic and roof photographs; pages 190-191 reproduce only main-floor phase superimpositions, with 1952 walls over 1875 and the 2014 master plan over 1952. It provides no upper-floor, attic or roof orthographic plan and is not added as model geometry.

The Triangle Casa Batllo monograph preview identifies dedicated attic and flat-roof chapters in its contents, but the accessible preview omits the attic chapter and exposes photographs/text rather than a complete orthographic upper plan.

Google Books verifies Rainer Zerbst's illustrated Taschen monograph bibliographically, but the accessible record does not expose the Casa Batllo plan plate at usable resolution or establish its survey date.

A student-uploaded plate reproduces separate attic and upper-floor diagrams, but omits the original plate's drafter, survey date and source citation. It is retained only as a search lead and cannot support current visitor geometry.
